newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate soars amid late speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate soars amid late speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates on Tuesday finished 430 basis points higher at 20.00 percent.
Dealers said a big player had deliberately withheld liquidity in order to force other dealers who needed cash to settle at high rates. "There was one hoarder who had all the cash," a trader said.
Dealers said the sharp rise was partly because rates on Monday had closed well below average trading levels for the day.
Analysts said speculative pressure on rates could also have been attempt to force up assignment rates at the primary central bank auction later in the day.
"The spike in secondary rates was speculative, but we still expect primary rates to fall," a fixed-income analyst said.
A Reuters survey of nine money-market traders forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 18.01 percent, or 71 basis points less than at last week's auction.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 9/32 in late trading to yield 6.38 percent, close to its lowest for the year.
Overnight rates on bank paper increased 250 basis points to 20.50 percent.
The central bank drained 151 million pesos from the market through a single repo.
Liquidity of 2.036 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
